record.original_question: Let V be a germ at 0 of an irreducible complex variety in C^n . For any small enough ǫ > 0, let E = Eǫ := V ∩ Rn ∩ {|z| < ǫ}. Define the extremal function UE on {|z| < ǫ} : UE (z) := sup{u(z); u ≤ 0 on E, 0 ≤ u ≤ 1 on {|z| < ǫ} The problem is to classify those V for which we have a constant A > 0 for which (α) UE (z) ≤ A|ℑz|, |z| < ǫ/2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a germ at $0$ of an irreducible complex analytic variety in $\mathbb{C}^n$. For all sufficiently small $\varepsilon > 0$, set
$$E = E_\varepsilon := V \cap \mathbb{R}^n \cap \{z \in \mathbb{C}^n : |z| < \varepsilon\},$$
and define the extremal (Siciak–Zaharyuta type) function on the ball $\{|z| < \varepsilon\}$ by
$$U_E(z) := \sup\{u(z) : u \text{ plurisubharmonic on } \{|z|<\varepsilon\},\ u \le 0 \text{ on } E,\ 0 \le u \le 1 \text{ on } \{|z|<\varepsilon\}\}.$$
Here $\Im z$ denotes the imaginary part of $z \in \mathbb{C}^n$ and $|\cdot|$ is the Euclidean norm.

Classify (give a necessary and sufficient geometric characterization of) those germs $V$ for which there exists a constant $A > 0$ such that
$$U_E(z) \le A\,|\Im z| \qquad \text{for all } |z| < \varepsilon/2.$$
artifact.status_search_result: A web search located related work on extremal plurisubharmonic functions of linear growth on algebraic varieties (Meise–Taylor–Vogt, Math. Z. 1995) and surveys in weighted pluripotential theory, but no source was found that explicitly classifies the germs of irreducible complex varieties for which the local extremal function $U_E$ is bounded linearly by $|\Im z|$. The status of this specific classification problem could not be conclusively determined.

status_evidence.title: Extremal plurisubharmonic functions of linear growth on algebraic varieties
status_evidence.snippet: For irreducible analytic subvarieties of dimension 1 ≤ m < n, characterizations are given for when the variety is algebraic in terms of extremal plurisubharmonic functions.
status_evidence.claim: Related results on linear growth of extremal psh functions exist but do not give the specific classification asked here.

status_evidence.title: Weighted Pluripotential Theory (Levenberg notes)
status_evidence.snippet: Surveys extremal functions in pluripotential theory.
status_evidence.claim: General surveys do not record a resolution of the classification problem.
